# 0.14.0 — scoped signal entities, a migration command, and a generation hot path

13 October 2026. Minor on **0.13.0**.

Two things need action after upgrading. `objective.signals[].entities` values are now stage-scoped, so `Hostname` becomes `Host::Hostname` — and `opentide migrate vocab-scope` does that for you. `response.responders` is no longer a vocabulary, so a value that could not validate under 0.13.0 now does.

Documentation and export generation are dramatically faster. A corpus that previously exceeded a one-hour CI job timeout now completes, which makes the deploy stage reachable again.

## Install

```bash
pip install opentide==0.14.0
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide migrate vocab-scope --apply
opentide generate schemas templates vocabs snippets
opentide validate --strict
```

## Breaking

- **`objective.signals[].entities` is stage-scoped.** An authored value is `<stage>::<key>`. Seven of the 28 entity keys are defined under two stages — `Account`, `User`, `Authentication`, `Token`, `Permissions`, `Email` and `API Call` — so a bare key name could not say whether a signal keyed on a **host** account or a **cloud** account. That is a real detection distinction: different telemetry, a different data contract, often a different platform. The enum carried 28 values where the vocabulary defines 35; it now carries all 35. Stage identifiers are capitalised to `Host`, `Network` and `Cloud`, matching the convention `threat.surface` already uses. Vocabulary entry keys are unchanged, so the `signal.entities::1.0` pin is unaffected. See [RFC 0005](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/specifications/blob/main/rfcs/0005-scoped-signal-entities.md).
- **`response.responders` is no longer a vocabulary.** The shipped `responders` vocabulary had `keys = []` while both rule revisions pinned the field to it, so every authored value failed validation and **no instance could clear it** — vocabularies are not locally extensible. One corpus reported 483 unclearable findings from two values. The field is now free text, defaulted from `[deployment] default_responders` — a key that shipped in the configuration template and in the spec but was read by no code at all, so the documented fallback never actually happened. The vocabulary file is removed.

## Added

- **`opentide migrate vocab-scope`** re-prefixes authored values for every stage-scoped field, not just the new one. Three properties make it safe on a real corpus:
  - **Nothing is guessed.** A bare key defined under several stages is reported with its candidates and left untouched; only an implied single-stage prefix or a stage-casing fix is applied. Exits 2 while anything is left for a human, so CI cannot mistake a partial migration for success.
  - **Only the declared field is touched.** Values are located by path through the document, not by leaf key name — a Sentinel platform block also carries a key called `entities`, holding entity *mappings*, and a name-based rewrite would corrupt it.
  - **Formatting survives.** Each value is replaced over the exact span its scalar occupies, so comments, block scalars, key order, quoting style and flow sequences are preserved. Every file is re-parsed and compared against the plan before it is written.

- **`generate --help` names the four positional phases.** `schemas`, `templates`, `vocabs` and `snippets` are accepted, but Typer renders the sub-app's help string rather than the callback docstring — which already named them — so the only place the list appeared was an error string you had to trigger deliberately. Naming the cheap phases is the documented remedy for a stale editor schema after a contract change, so the right command was previously unguessable.
- **`generate` reports what each phase costs**, and names the slowest. A run that overran a CI job timeout emitted no phase boundary and no timing, so a killed job gave no way to tell whether it was 10% or 90% through — which is why the 0.13.0 report could not narrow its own blocker down. Timing is recorded even when a phase raises.

## Fixed

- **Documentation and export generation no longer rescan the catalogue per object.** `childs()` walked every model on every call, while all of its callers are per-object: the table exporter per row, the documentation catalogue per signal, and `relations_downstream()` recursively at every level. Cost therefore grew with the square of the corpus. It is now a reverse index built once per catalogue generation — **68× faster** on a 1497-object corpus. This one function is the root cause behind both a `generate docs` phase that exceeded a one-hour CI job timeout and a `generate exports` phase measured at 395s.
- **A relation could be attributed to the wrong object.** `childs()` matched a model id against reference values with a substring test, so a short non-UUID id matched a longer one containing it: `o-1` matched a signal referencing `o-186`, returning 113 spurious children. Comparison is now by equality. UUID-shaped ids could not trigger this; any other id scheme could.
- **`validate` and `generate` agreed to disagree.** `get_vocab_entry()` stripped the stage prefix unconditionally before lookup while `is_valid()` checked the raw value first, so a repository could be green on `validate` and still produce degraded documentation. Both now resolve through one raw-first helper. Three `Security::*` surface keys resolved to a *different* entry under the stripping path and three more missed entirely; all six are reachable now.
- **`check_status` resolved a status by name, not by strategy**, so renaming a configured deployment status silently took the wrong branch. It now resolves the strategy, and raises typed errors in place of a bare `Exception`.
- **The test suite could rewrite the repository under test.** Git tests ran `git` with `cwd=` set to a temporary repository but inherited the environment, and `GIT_DIR` overrides `cwd`. When `git push` exported `GIT_DIR` to its hooks and a hook ran the suite, the fixtures committed and checked out branches **in the real repository** — producing a commit that deleted 890 files. The environment is now sanitised for every test, with a collection-time guard so the hazard cannot return silently. This affects contributors, not released behaviour.

## Verify

```bash
opentide migrate vocab-scope            # dry run; names every rewrite and every ambiguity
opentide migrate vocab-scope --apply
opentide generate schemas templates vocabs snippets
opentide validate --strict
```

The generated `objective` schema should carry 35 stage-prefixed `entities` values, with `Host::Account` and `Cloud::Account` both present and distinct:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib
schema = json.loads(pathlib.Path(".opentide/schemas/objective.1.0.schema.json").read_text())
enum = schema["$defs"]["DetectionSignal"]["properties"]["entities"]["items"]["enum"]
print(len(enum), "values;", sum("::" in v for v in enum), "stage-prefixed")
print("Host::Account" in enum, "Cloud::Account" in enum)
PY
```

## Thanks

The defect report behind most of this release was measured end to end on a 1276-object corpus with the full pipeline run on a throwaway project. Two of its items were retracted on review — one by the reporter, one by us — and that is exactly what a good report looks like.
